questions.question: A child is riding a bicycle near your vehicle. What should you do?

options.text: Expect the child to control the bicycle perfectly.

questions.explanation: Children on bicycles may do unexpected things. They often change direction suddenly. Children and bicycles are small and hard to see.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, you must yield to drivers who arrived before you.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, yield to drivers who arrived first. Wait your turn before entering the intersection.

questions.question: After a train passes at a railroad crossing, what should you do?

options.text: Wait until the signal lights stop flashing.

questions.explanation: After a train passes, watch for a second train on any track. Do not drive forward until all gates are up and all warning lights have stopped flashing.

questions.question: You have a green light and there are pedestrians in the intersection. What should you do?

options.text: You have the right-of-way over pedestrians.

questions.explanation: When you have a green light, you must still yield to pedestrians and other vehicles in the intersection. Drivers must yield to pedestrians when turning on a green light.

questions.question: In fog, should you use high beam headlights to see better?
questions.explanation: In fog, use low beam headlights or fog lights. Do not use high beams.

questions.question: You are following a large truck on the freeway. How should you drive?

options.text: Drive close behind the truck in bad weather so you can see ahead.
Stay farther back than you would behind a regular car.
Stay one car length behind so the driver can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther back than you would behind a regular car.
questions.explanation: If you follow too closely behind a truck, the driver cannot see you. Staying too close is dangerous because you won't have time to stop if the truck stops suddenly.

questions.question: Oncoming headlights are blinding you at night. What should you do?

options.text: Look toward the right edge of the road.
Switch your lights to high beams.
Flip your lights on and off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: If oncoming headlights are blinding you, look toward the right edge of the road instead of ahead. This keeps your vehicle safe until the other car passes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Bicyclists use hand and arm signals instead of turn signals. A left arm straight out means the bicyclist is turning left.

questions.question: What is a "No zone"?

options.text: The blind spot around a large vehicle
An area for motor vehicles only

questions.correctAnswerText: The blind spot around a large vehicle
questions.explanation: A "No zone" is the blind spot around trucks and large vehicles where the driver cannot see you. Avoid staying in these areas.

questions.question: When driving behind another vehicle at night, what should you do?

options.text: Use high beam headlights until you are 10 feet away.

questions.explanation: Use high beams only in rural areas when no other cars are near. Switch to low beams when following another driver.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a U-turn. You may see this sign where traffic comes from both directions.

questions.question: You are driving at night and another vehicle is coming toward you. Your headlights should be:

options.text: Off. Use your parking lights instead.
On high beam or low beam—either is okay.

questions.explanation: Do not use high beams when another vehicle is near you at night. Use low beams to keep everyone safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a steep hill is coming.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The safest speed for a residential area.
The safest speed for leaving a highway.
The safest speed for entering a highway.
The safest speed for a work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: The safest speed for leaving a highway.
questions.explanation: This sign shows the safe speed to drive when exiting a highway (for example, 30 mph).

questions.question: When passing another vehicle on a two-lane road, you should:

options.text: Move back to your lane when you are safely ahead of the other vehicle.
Stay in the left lane if you plan to turn left.
Return to the right side of the road right away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move back to your lane when you are safely ahead of the other vehicle.
questions.explanation: After passing, move back to the right side of the road when there is enough space between you and the vehicle you passed.

questions.question: You should not use your horn:

options.text: When you cannot see far ahead.
If you might hit another vehicle.

questions.explanation: Do not use your horn around blind pedestrians. It may confuse them. Instead, slow down and wait until it is safe to pass.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road ahead turns sharply right, then left.
The road ahead turns sharply left, then right.
The road ahead curves to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead turns sharply right, then left.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you the road will turn sharply to the right and then to the left.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, it is safe to return to your lane if you:

options.text: Cannot see the vehicle directly to your right.
See the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
Have passed the other vehicle's front bumper.

questions.correctAnswerText: See the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Before moving back to your lane, make sure you are far enough ahead. When you can see both headlights in your rearview mirror, you have enough room to move back safely.

questions.question: You may drive across a dashed white line:

options.text: When it is safe to change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it is safe to change lanes.
questions.explanation: Dashed white lines separate lanes going the same direction. You can cross them to pass if it is safe.

questions.question: A blood alcohol level of 0.02 percent:

options.text: Has no effect on your driving.
Does not put other drivers at risk.
Doubles your chance of a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Doubles your chance of a crash.
questions.explanation: For every 0.02 percent increase in blood alcohol, a driver's risk of a fatal crash nearly doubles.

questions.question: When making a right turn on a green light, you must:

options.text: Stop and look for police cars.

questions.explanation: You can turn right or left at a green light unless a sign says you cannot. When you turn, you must let other cars and pedestrians in the intersection go first.

questions.question: When driving in a construction zone:

options.text: Assume construction workers will get out of your way.

questions.explanation: Construction zones have unexpected hazards. Drive very carefully to protect yourself, other drivers, and construction workers.

questions.question: A red arrow pointing right on a traffic light means you:

options.text: Can turn right after you slow down and check for traffic.
Cannot turn right until the light turns green.
Can turn right after you stop completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cannot turn right until the light turns green.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means stop. You must wait until a green light or green arrow appears. Do not turn when a red arrow is showing.

questions.question: To turn left from a multilane one-way street onto another one-way street, start your turn from:

options.text: The lane closest to the left side.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to the left side.
questions.explanation: When turning left from a one-way street onto another one-way street, begin your turn from the far left lane.

questions.question: The best way to avoid hydroplaning is to:

options.text: Keep your tires in good condition.
Drive slower when roads are wet or slushy.

questions.explanation: On wet roads, your car needs more distance to stop and may skid when turning quickly. Do not use cruise control on wet or icy roads. Slow down and drive carefully.

questions.question: Roads become most slippery:

options.text: After it has rained for an hour or more.
During the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain.
questions.explanation: Roads are very slippery at the start of rain because water brings oil from the asphalt to the surface. This is worse in hot weather, when more oil rises to the road.

questions.question: When driving on wet pavement, remember:

options.text: Roads are very slippery right when rain starts.

questions.explanation: Wet roads are very slippery, especially right after rain starts. When driving on wet roads, your tires are on a thin layer of oil, dirt, and water. Slow down in heavy rain, standing water, or slush to keep your wheels from sliding.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Do not speed on wet roads.
Keep tires filled to the correct pressure.

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning occurs when your car slides on a thin layer of water between your tires and the road. Tires with low pressure or bad tread increase this risk. Speeding also increases the risk.

questions.question: Traffic signs and pavement markings:

options.text: Must be followed only when other cars are present.
Must be followed only when a police officer is watching.

questions.explanation: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings control traffic flow. They tell drivers about road conditions and help guide them safely. Always obey traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings.

questions.question: You can help the driver behind you stay a safe distance away by:

options.text: Driving 10 mph faster than the car behind you.
Driving 10 mph slower than the car behind you.

questions.explanation: It is hard to keep a safe distance from your car. You can help by driving at a steady speed and signaling turns, lane changes, and when you slow down ahead of time.
